title: 2×2 rib fingerless mitts in aran wool
subtitle: Quick fingerless mitts in aran weight with a gusseted thumb.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts in aran-weight wool worked entirely in 2×2 rib, with a gusseted thumb for a better anatomical fit. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm. A quick knit at aran weight.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 9th series (1880s), §Ribbed mitts. The ribbed fingerless mitt with a gusseted thumb is among the most common Victorian hand-knitting patterns; 2×2 rib variants appear in both Weldon's and Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870), §Knitted gloves.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 24 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in 2×2 rib slightly stretched on 5 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb construction where a wedge of extra stitches is increased over several rounds alongside the thumb position. The gusset stitches are set aside on waste yarn while the hand continues, then worked as the thumb. The gusseted shape matches the natural angle of the thumb and gives a more comfortable fit than an afterthought thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

An increase worked by lifting the horizontal strand between two stitches with the left needle and knitting into the back of it. M1L lifts the strand from left to right (left-leaning); M1R lifts it from right to left (right-leaning).

content.text: Fingerless mitts in aran-weight wool, worked in 2×2 rib throughout with a gusseted thumb, sized to fit hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
The construction is seamless, worked in the round using
magic loop
on a long circular. The thumb uses a
gusseted thumb

, which increases a small wedge of stitches beside the thumb position over 6 rounds and gives a better fit at the base of the thumb than the afterthought method. Aran weight at 5 mm needles works up faster than DK and produces a warm fabric. Budget about 120 g (260 m / 285 yards) for both mitts. The rib stretches well across the knuckles, making these good for driving or cycling.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 120 g (about 260 m / 285 yards) of aran-weight wool
items.substitutions: Any aran or worsted-weight wool. The rib relies on the elasticity of wool; a high-wool content gives the best fit.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4 — 1 for the beginning of the round, 2 to flank the gusset, 1 spare

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 40 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for holding the gusset stitches

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 24 rounds to 10 cm over 2×2 rib slightly stretched on 5 mm needles. The slightly-stretched measurement matters because 2×2 rib pulls in heavily when relaxed. Measure the swatch with the rib pulled out to about the width it will sit on a hand.

If your gauge is 19 stitches per 10 cm rather than 18, the size M mitt will be about 1 cm narrower at the palm. That tightens the knuckle fit noticeably. Try 5.5 mm needles if your tension runs tight.
Stitches used

items.name: M1L
items.qty: make 1 left (lift strand from left to right, knit into back)

items.name: M1R
items.qty: make 1 right (lift strand from right to left, knit into back)

content.text: Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 32 (36, 40) stitches. All sizes are multiples of 4 so the 2×2 rib joins cleanly. At 5 mm needles for 40 stitches, pull off about 35 cm of tail before starting.
Join to work in the round, placing the beginning-of-round marker. Work 2×2 rib (k2, p2 every round) for 20 (22, 24) rounds. The cuff measures about 8 (9, 10) cm.
Thumb gusset
The gusset sits at the beginning of the round on a right mitt. Place a gusset marker before stitch 1 and after stitch 2 (the 2 knit stitches at the start of the rib pattern).
Increase round 1: SM,
M1R
, k2 (the two gusset stitches), M1L, SM, continue in 2×2 rib to end. 2 stitches increased. Gusset now has 4 stitches.
Work 2 plain rib rounds.
Increase round 2: SM, M1R, work gusset stitches in rib, M1L, SM, continue in rib to end. 2 stitches increased. Gusset has 6 stitches.
Work 2 plain rib rounds. Repeat the increase-then-2-plain pattern twice more. After the final increase round, the gusset holds 10 (10, 12) stitches.
Stitch count check-in after gusset: you should have 42 (46, 52) stitches on the needles: 32 (36, 40) hand stitches plus 10 (10, 12) gusset stitches.
Set aside the gusset

Slip the 10 (10, 12) gusset stitches onto waste yarn. Using backward-loop cast-on, cast on 2 stitches over the gap to maintain the rib pattern at the thumb position. Continue in 2×2 rib across the hand.
Hand above gusset
Work in 2×2 rib for 14 (16, 18) rounds. The total hand length is about 18 (20, 22) cm. Bind off in 2×2 rib.
Stitch count check-in before bind-off: you should have 34 (38, 42) stitches: the 32 (36, 40) hand stitches plus the 2 bridging cast-on stitches.
Thumb
Return the 10 (10, 12) gusset stitches to the needles and pick up 2 stitches from the bridging cast-on. Total: 12 (12, 14) thumb stitches.
Join the yarn and work 10 (12, 12) rounds of 2×2 rib. Bind off in rib.
Mirror your second mitt

Place the gusset markers at the end of the round instead of the beginning for the second mitt. Hold the first mitt palm-out: the thumb sits on your right. The second mitt's thumb should sit on your left.
Common faults
Gusset pulls the rib out of alignment: the bridging cast-on stitches do not align with the 2×2 rib pattern. Check that the 2 cast-on stitches over the gap land on knit columns, not purl columns.
Thumb too tight at the base: the gusset was set aside too early. Work the gusset increase rounds until the gusset is at least 3 cm wide before setting it aside.
Two mitts for the same hand: the gusset sits at opposite ends of the round on left and right mitts.
Finishing
Weave in all yarn tails on the wrong side. Close any small holes at the thumb base with a few stitches using the tapestry needle.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. The aran-weight rib dries quickly.
What to try next
The gusseted thumb technique used here transfers directly to a full aran mitten. From there, adding a simple cable column down the back of the hand is the natural decoration at this skill level.
